## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by reddish-brown to orange-brown forewings with darker wavy markings and a reddish line or margin that gives the species its name. In Florida, it is found in hammocks, forests, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plants and serve as part of the food web for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
